office_does: The Pierce County Prosecuting Attorney decides which crimes to charge and prosecutes them, and serves as the county's civil legal counsel.
race_blurb: With Prosecutor Mary Robnett retiring, her Chief Criminal Deputy Coreen Schnepf faces former Superior Court Judge Bryan Chushcoff. Both run on enforcement; Chushcoff says the office's management is failing on charging and backlog, while Schnepf runs on her trial record and continuity.

candidates.summary: Chief Criminal Deputy in the Pierce County Prosecutor's Office and a 20-year trial prosecutor, endorsed by outgoing Prosecutor Mary Robnett.
highlights: Chief Criminal Deputy since 2024, leading a 180-person criminal division; earlier led the Domestic Violence and Human Trafficking Unit [S2][S8]
Says she 'has no patience for crime of any kind' and will hold accountable those who make life 'challenging, expensive, and unsafe' [S8]
Would add focus on stolen cars and organized retail theft and build digital-evidence capacity [S3]
Endorsed by Robnett, Legislative District Democrats, Mainstream Republicans, WEA and three IAFF locals [S4][S6]

safety.basis: Repeatedly runs on convictions for violent crime, more focus on car and retail theft and 'no patience for crime of any kind'; states no position on diversion, bail, policing levels or treatment, and an endorser describes a compassionate approach.

experience.basis: Twenty-year career prosecutor and current chief criminal deputy, running as the incumbent-backed successor; first run for office.

spending.basis: Pledges to 'show you what the office delivers for every dollar' and hold town halls; a single accountability line with no call for new spending.

candidates.summary: Former Pierce County Superior Court judge (1997-2025, per his campaign), running on fixing the office's charging rates, felony filings and case backlog.
highlights: Says he served seven terms as a Superior Court judge, including two terms as presiding judge over 100 employees and a $14 million budget [S2][S8]
Cites the decline-to-charge rate rising from 8% of bookings (2019) to 15.3% (2024) and a growing felony backlog [S3]
Says delays shift jail, medical and legal costs to taxpayers and pledges staff accountability, reorganization and training [S8]
Endorsed by the Pierce County Republican Party, the Tacoma Police Union and the deputy sheriffs' guild [S4][S5]

safety.basis: Criticizes the rising decline-to-charge rate, falling felony filings and a communication gap with law enforcement, framed as management failures; no stated position on diversion, bail or sentencing.

experience.basis: Campaign and statement cite 28 years (1997-2025) on the Superior Court plus presiding-judge and statewide court leadership, presented as proven leadership (not independently verified).

spending.basis: Calls the office's core failure management, wants performance data to drive strategy, and says backlog costs fall on taxpayers; the one counterweight is a call for more funding to retain experienced staff.
